seams.name: Value Representation & Poison/Undefined-Bit Seam
seams.lhs_premise_type: Mathematical Nat / Int values bounded by usizeMax (2^64 - 1) in MirVal.usize
seams.rhs_premise_type: Fixed-width two's-complement BitVec 64 machine words (with poison/undef bit masks in AnLLVM/SSALike)
seams.why_definitions_fail_to_meet: Anneal MIR evaluates arithmetic in mathematical Nat with explicit overflow assertions (`x + y <= usizeMax`), whereas LLVM IR and x86-64 instructions operate on modular `BitVec 64` rings where `BitVec.ofNat 64 (x + y) = x + y` holds only under a non-overflow side condition.
seams.bridge_adapter: wordRepresentsNat (w : BitVec 64) (n : Nat) : Prop := w.toNat = n /\ n <= usizeMax; seam1_mir_to_ssa_pre_bridge
seams.tcb_placement: trusted/lean/Trusted/ (value injection relation must be part of the trusted target boundary; bridge proof lives in untrusted theory/)

seams.boundary: Link 1 (Anneal MIR Memory) -> Link 2/3 (SSA Registers & Flat Address Space)
seams.name: Memory Model & Provenance Erasing Injection Seam
seams.lhs_premise_type: Typed allocation store `AllocId -> Option MirVal` with generation tags (`localGens`) and frame IDs (`frameId`)
seams.rhs_premise_type: Promoted SSA virtual registers (`RegId -> BitVec 64`) and flat byte-addressed hardware memory (`BitVec 64 -> UInt8`)
seams.why_definitions_fail_to_meet: MIR stack locals whose addresses are taken (`let r = &x; *r` in `alloc_passthrough`) live in disjoint logical allocations indexed by `(frameId, LocalId, gen)`, whereas SROA/mem2reg eliminates the allocation completely or lowers it into `[rsp + disp]` in a shared 64-bit address space.
seams.tcb_placement: Untrusted theory/ for SROA/mem2reg promotion; trusted/lean/Trusted/ only for top-level initial memory well-formedness

seams.boundary: Link 2 (Big-Step Functional / CFG SSA) -> Link 4 (Small-Step Variable-Length Byte Fetch)
seams.name: Control-Flow, Fuel, and Variable-Length Instruction Fetch Seam
seams.lhs_premise_type: Structured CFG basic-block evaluation (`evalSsaPostO3 : BitVec 64 -> BitVec 64 -> MirOutcome (BitVec 64)`)
seams.rhs_premise_type: Small-step byte-indexed `rip` state machine (`runX86 : Nat -> X86State -> Option X86State`) with variable instruction lengths (1, 2, 4, and 7 bytes)
seams.why_definitions_fail_to_meet: Big-step/CFG semantics index control flow by abstract `BlockId` without code layout, whereas `X86State` fetches raw `UInt8` bytes at `rip + 0#64 .. rip + 6#64` and advances `rip` by `4#64, 2#64, 7#64, 4#64, 7#64, 4#64, 1#64`. Furthermore, coupling `decodeX86At` to the full `X86State` record prevents `simp` from reusing decode lemmas after register updates.
seams.bridge_adapter: loadedAt m codeBase fixtureMachineBytes + state-decoupled `decodeX86At (codeMem : BitVec 64 -> UInt8) (rip : BitVec 64)` + existential step witness `exists k, runX86 k m_init = some m_final`
seams.tcb_placement: trusted/lean/Trusted/ defines `X86State`, `stepX86`, `runX86`, and `loadedAt`; per-function `k = 7` execution proofs live in untrusted theory/

seams.boundary: Link 2 (Unlimited SSA Locals) -> Link 3/4 (System V AMD64 ABI Calling Convention)
seams.name: Calling Convention, Flag Clobber, and Stack Return Seam
seams.lhs_premise_type: Positional MIR local slots (`_1 = x`, `_2 = y`, `_0 = ret`)
seams.rhs_premise_type: System V AMD64 physical register assignment (`rdi = arg0`, `rsi = arg1`, `rax = ret`), hardware `CF` flag dataflow (`cmpq` -> `cmovaeq`), return address at `readStack64 (regs .rsp)`, `rsp` post-increment (`+ 8#64`), and callee-saved register preservation (`rbx, rbp, r12..r15`)
seams.why_definitions_fail_to_meet: MIR has no concept of physical caller/callee-saved registers, condition-code flags (`CF`), or return addresses stored on the stack frame.
seams.tcb_placement: trusted/lean/Trusted/ (System V ABI entry/exit contract is part of the machine-level theorem statement)

seams.name: Observable Events and Termination Outcome Seam
seams.rhs_premise_type: Concrete machine state transition `runX86 k m_init = some m_final /\ m_final.rip = retAddr`
seams.why_definitions_fail_to_meet: Hardware machine states do not carry a sum-type constructor `.returned`; normal return is observed by `m_final.rip` reaching the caller's `retAddr` with `rsp = rsp_0 + 8` and the return value in `m_final.regs .rax`.
seams.bridge_adapter: HighLevelPost arg0 arg1 (m_final.regs .rax) relating `m_final.regs .rax` back to `evalMirAddBounded st_mir = .returned (m_final.regs .rax).toNat`
